messages:
Maria Choi: Heads-up — after the RBAC tweak to the `data-plane` serviceaccount in the EU private cluster, we're seeing intermittent KMS decrypt failures from model-serving pods (403). Impact: canary + 2 prod pods. Anyone picking this up?
sec-bot: ALERT: KMS_DECRYPT_FAILURE spike detected (count=12) cluster=eu-priv severity=high — related commits: 8a7f3b2
Ajay Kapoor: when was the RBAC change applied (timestamp/PR)? can we rollback quickly if needed? any config diff? :eyes:
Maria Choi: PR #1428 merged ~2026-03-22T09:12Z (commit 8a7f3b2). Patch was tightening rolebindings for `data-plane` SA to remove broad kms:decrypt on the shared-keystore key. I have the kubectl patch we applied: 
```
kubectl -n models patch rolebinding data-plane-kms --patch '{"subjects":[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"data-plane","namespace":"models"}]}'
```
Ellie Ops: grabbing logs now. Quick excerpt from pod `model-serve-7f6b` shows: 
```
2026-03-22T09:18:03Z ERROR keymanager: decrypt failed: rpc error: code=PermissionDenied desc="caller serviceAccount:models/data-plane missing kms.keys.decrypt"
2026-03-22T09:18:03Z INFO token: svcacct token fetched ok
```
So token fetch works but KMS denies.
Samir Patel: two quick hypotheses: 1) RBAC/IAM change removed the IAM binding that allows that SA to call KMS; 2) network-policy blocked egress to the KMS control plane endpoint (so key service sees a different principal or no mTLS). Which KMS are we using for EU-priv — HSM-backed internal KMS gateway, right?
Maria Choi: correct — it's our internal HSM-gateway in the EU onprem colo (keystore-proxy svc). The RBAC change was purely k8s RoleBinding but we also recently tightened egress netpolicy in `models` ns to deny metadata/proxy egress.
Ajay Kapoor: can you run `kubectl get networkpolicy -n models -o yaml` and `kubectl exec -n models model-serve-7f6b -- curl -v https://keystore.internal.local/health` to verify reachability?
Ellie Ops: ran checks: `keystore` is reachable from the pod, 200 on /health. But keystore logs show a 403 against the wrapped key service with principal `system:serviceaccount:models:data-plane@cluster.local` missing permission. I'll pull the keystore audit entries now (taking a minute).
sec-bot: AUDIT: keystore-gateway.log entries found: 2026-03-22T09:17:58Z principal=system:serviceaccount:models:data-plane action=decrypt result=DENIED reason="policy:missing-iam-binding"
Samir Patel: okay that points at IAM/policy layer — RBAC change likely removed the binding to the HSM key wrapper. Two mitigations: 1) temporarily re-add the previous RoleBinding to restore service availability, 2) run a least-privileged quickfix: create a namespaced role that grants only decrypt for the specific key and scope it to the canary pods, then schedule a proper audit.
Maria Choi: I can revert the rolebinding patch immediately if we agree. Rollback command: 
```
git revert 8a7f3b2 -m "revert tightened rolebinding until IAM mapping validated" && ./deploy-scripts/kubectl-apply.sh -f deploy/roles/data-plane-kms.yaml
```
Ajay Kapoor: +1 to revert for availability. Post-rollback we need to run an audit to map k8s subject -> id token -> keystore principal so we can make the least-privileged binding. Also record in incident tracker INC-2026-033. I'll own the rollback if Maria gives :thumbsup:.
Maria Choi: doing rollback now. tagging @Ellie Ops for postmortem logs.
Ellie Ops: FYI I'm extracting the keystore audit logs and KMS gateway policy diffs. Early glance shows the SA-to-principal mapping change happened at the same commit that updated the RBAC patch (PR#1428). I'll attach the audit snippet to the ticket. Also recommend we add an automated pre-deploy check: simulate a decrypt request in the canary after RBAC changes.
Samir Patel: long term we should add a fallback in the keystore-proxy: a node-level wrapped key that allows node bootstrap operations if the principal is unrecognized (audit-forwarded and rate-limited). That reduces outage blast radius for RBAC mistakes. Also suggest a bolt-on canary: `kubectl run --rm canary-decrypt -n models --image=debug -- curl` as part of the rolebinding CI job.
Ajay Kapoor: after rollback, please confirm vault/keystore shows decrypt logs success. If good, we'll re-open a change window to apply a least-privileged binding + CI test.
sec-bot: ACTION: rollback started by Maria Choi at 2026-03-22T09:22:05Z. Monitoring for decrypt success...
Maria Choi: rollback applied, pods re-deploying. Watching logs.
Ellie Ops: post-rollback keystore audit shows `result=ALLOWED` for the same principal at 09:23:11Z. Two prod pods reported recovered. I'll attach full audit and suggested minimal role to the incident.
Ajay Kapoor: good. Create the follow-up PR to replace broad decrypt with a key-scoped binding and add the canary test. Tagging security reviewers.
Maria Choi: created INC-2026-033 and PR #1432 (wip). Thanks everyone. We'll run a short postmortem and update the private-deploy hardening checklist to require keystore audit playback for any RBAC/netpol changes.
sec-bot: RESOLVED: KMS_DECRYPT spike cleared at 2026-03-22T09:24:35Z (duration ~7m). Incident owner: Ajay Kapoor.
